Gamma Transition Selection Rules

Concise reference for nuclear electromagnetic transitions.

1. Definitions

  • J,πJ, \piJ,π: Nuclear spin and parity
  • LLL: Multipolarity order (photon angular momentum)
  • ΔJ\Delta JΔJ: Spin change, ∣Ji−Jf∣|J_i - J_f|∣Ji​−Jf​∣
  • Δπ\Delta \piΔπ: Parity change (Yes/No)
  • Multipolarity Designations:
    • D (Dipole, L=1L=1L=1): E1, M1
    • Q (Quadrupole, L=2L=2L=2): E2, M2
    • O (Octupole, L=3L=3L=3): E3, M3
    • H (Hexadecapole, L=4L=4L=4): E4, M4
  • Notation:
    • Comma (,) = OR (alternative multipolarities)
    • Plus (+) = AND (mixed multipolarity)

2. Fundamental Principles

Angular Momentum Conservation

The triangle inequality restricts the possible multipolarity LLL:

∣Ji−Jf∣≤L≤Ji+Jf |J_i - J_f| \leq L \leq J_i + J_f ∣Ji​−Jf​∣≤L≤Ji​+Jf​

Example: For Ji=Jf=1/2J_i = J_f = 1/2Ji​=Jf​=1/2, quadrupole (L≥2L \geq 2L≥2) transitions are strictly forbidden geometrically.

Parity Selection

  • Electric (ELLL): Δπ=(−1)L\Delta \pi = (-1)^LΔπ=(−1)L (Parity changes for odd LLL)
  • Magnetic (MLLL): Δπ=(−1)L+1\Delta \pi = (-1)^{L+1}Δπ=(−1)L+1 (Parity changes for even LLL)

Note: 0→00 \to 00→0 single photon emission is strictly forbidden.

Dominance of Lowest Multipolarity (Practical Rules)

While geometry permits a range of LLL, nuclear transition probabilities dictate which are actually observed.

  1. Weisskopf Estimates: Probability decreases by factor of ≈105\approx 10^5≈105 for each unit increase in LLL.
  2. Dominance Rule: Transitions proceed via the lowest permitted multipolarity (LminL_{min}Lmin​).
  3. Mixing:
    • Lmin+1L_{min} + 1Lmin​+1 mixing is common (e.g., M1+E2).
    • Lmin+2L_{min} + 2Lmin​+2 or higher is generally negligible (<10−5< 10^{-5}<10−5 branching).
    • Practical implication: Multipolarity assignments like M2+E3 are only practical when Dipole (L=1L=1L=1) is forbidden by selection rules (i.e., ΔJ≥2\Delta J \geq 2ΔJ≥2).

5. Mixed Multipolarities

Common mixing patterns constrained by the dominance rule:

  • D+Q (E1+M2 or M1+E2): ΔJ=0,1\Delta J = 0, 1ΔJ=0,1
  • Q+O (E2+M3 or M2+E3): ΔJ=2\Delta J = 2ΔJ=2
  • M1+E2: ΔJ=0,1\Delta J = 0, 1ΔJ=0,1; Δπ=No\Delta \pi = \text{No}Δπ=No
  • E1+M2: ΔJ=0,1\Delta J = 0, 1ΔJ=0,1; Δπ=Yes\Delta \pi = \text{Yes}Δπ=Yes
  • E2+M3: ΔJ=2\Delta J = 2ΔJ=2; Δπ=No\Delta \pi = \text{No}Δπ=No
  • M2+E3: ΔJ=2\Delta J = 2ΔJ=2; Δπ=Yes\Delta \pi = \text{Yes}Δπ=Yes

  2. M1+E2 transition from/to 5/2+5/2^+5/2+:

    • ΔJ=0,1\Delta J = 0, 1ΔJ=0,1; Δπ=No\Delta \pi = \text{No}Δπ=No

6. Capture Transitions

Primary γ\gammaγ transitions from neutron/proton capture resonances are physically dominated by the lowest multipoles (E1, M1, E2). Higher orders are kinetically and statistically suppressed.

  • D (E1, M1): ΔJ=0,1\Delta J = 0, 1ΔJ=0,1; Δπ=Yes or No\Delta \pi = \text{Yes or No}Δπ=Yes or No
  • E2: ΔJ=2\Delta J = 2ΔJ=2; Δπ=No\Delta \pi = \text{No}Δπ=No

Examples: Deducing JπJ^\piJπ Final from Multipolarity and JπJ^\piJπ Initial

Primary transition from 5/2+5/2^+5/2+ initial via D or E2:

  • D (E1, M1): Final 3/2±,5/2±,7/2±3/2±, 5/2±, 7/2±3/2±,5/2±,7/2±
  • E2: Final 1/2+,9/2+1/2^+, 9/2^+1/2+,9/2+
  • Combination: 1/2+,3/2±,5/2±,7/2±,9/2+1/2^+, 3/2±, 5/2±, 7/2±, 9/2^+1/2+,3/2±,5/2±,7/2±,9/2+

Primary transition from 7/2−7/2^-7/2− initial via D or E2:

  • D (E1, M1): Final 5/2±,7/2±,9/2±5/2±, 7/2±, 9/2±5/2±,7/2±,9/2±
  • E2: Final 3/2−,11/2−3/2^-, 11/2^-3/2−,11/2−
  • Combination: 3/2−,5/2±,7/2±,9/2±,11/2−3/2^-, 5/2±, 7/2±, 9/2±, 11/2^-3/2−,5/2±,7/2±,9/2±,11/2−

7. Practical Workflow: Intersection Logic

Deducing JπJ^\piJπ from Multiple Constraints

  1. List allowed JπJ^\piJπ from each constraint (primary feeding, secondary decays)
  2. Apply AND (intersection) across all constraints
  3. Result: Common JπJ^\piJπ values only

Note: Parentheses in ENSDF denote tentative assignments, e.g., (5/2+,7/2,9/2+)

Example 1: Fed by primary γ from 5/2-. Decay γ to 1/2+ and 5/2+

Fed by primary γ (D or E2): 1/2-, 3/2±, 5/2±, 7/2±, 9/2-

Decay γ to 1/2+ (D or E2): 1/2±, 3/2±, 5/2+

Decay γ to 5/2+ (D or E2): 1/2+, 3/2±, 5/2±, 7/2±, 9/2+

AND: 3/2±, 5/2+

Example 2: Fed by primary γ from 7/2-, 7/2+, and 5/2+

Fed by primary γ from 7/2- (D or E2): 3/2-, 5/2±, 7/2±, 9/2±, 11/2-

Fed by primary γ from 7/2+ (D or E2): 3/2+, 5/2±, 7/2±, 9/2±, 11/2+

Fed by primary γ from 5/2+ (D or E2): 1/2+, 3/2±, 5/2±, 7/2±, 9/2+

AND: 5/2±, 7/2±, 9/2+

Example 3: Fed by primary γ from 7/2+. Decay γ to 5/2+ (Lifetime unknown, RUL does not apply, M2 allowed)

Fed by primary γ (D or E2): 3/2+, 5/2±, 7/2±, 9/2±, 11/2+

Decay γ to 5/2+ (D or Q): 1/2±, 3/2±, 5/2±, 7/2±, 9/2±

AND: 3/2+, 5/2±, 7/2±, 9/2±
